category: AI core arXiv categories and cross-lists
title: AI papers in the arXiv announcement batch of Wed, 18 Nov 2026 — 9 papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from independently checkable technical discussion and public research artifacts, with category breadth as a secondary signal. Citation evidence is limited for this very new batch: Semantic Scholar showed zero citations and zero influential citations for all nine selected papers at the snapshot.

sections.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
sections.abstract: FastFrames redesigns video-diffusion decoding and cache updates, with the authors reporting 36 ms per frame for a 1.3B model on one B200 GPU and 45 ms for a 14B model on eight B200 GPUs.
sections.ranking_evidence: The official Apple research repository releases both FastFrames model sizes, and the paper received separate technical coverage from Papers with Code and AI Films Studio.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report replacing high-cost VAE decoding and KV-cache updates with lightweight alternatives, reducing end-to-end generation latency while retaining their reported quality comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors measure latency on B200 hardware and focus primarily on 480p; they note that 720p increases latency substantially and needs further optimization.

sections.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: Spool caches composable per-frame recurrent-state transformations so hybrid vision-language models can expire old video frames without replaying the full window, with the authors reporting a 6.6× geometric-mean reduction in p95 time-to-first-token and a 2.3-point average online-accuracy gain.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper has multiple independent technical explainers, including Bitware News and Crunch, and is cross-listed in two core AI categories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a training-free state-transition cache and supporting data structures/kernels, evaluated across hybrid VLMs and streaming-video benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that layer-wise state reconstruction is exact for cached updates but is not identical to rerunning the full network: retained layer inputs can still encode some expired-frame influence.

sections.title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models
sections.abstract: RSI-Prime packages 350 annotated model-training trajectories and applies decision-level loss masking; the authors report a 31.95% relative improvement for GLM-5.3 on PostTrainBench.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work has independent technical summaries from Franklineh and DEEKOYA AI, and it spans the core AI and machine-learning categories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors construct full experimental trajectories, annotate decision quality, and use selective supervision to teach models model-training decisions.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported benchmark result is for GLM-5.3 on PostTrainBench; broader validation across base models and training settings is not established by that result.

sections.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
sections.abstract: In a gameplay testbed, the authors let frozen LLM agents build their own context-based learning procedures from basic tools, a compute budget, and a general improvement goal, and report transfer across game tasks and 3D navigation.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper drew separate explanatory coverage from The Agent Times and Explainx, and is cross-listed in two core AI categories.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors study self-organized learning loops rather than prescribing an external optimization procedure, reporting that sufficiently capable agents improve in their gameplay setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The experiments use games and explicitly exclude access to real-world data, so the results do not establish open-ended self-improvement outside that controlled testbed.

sections.title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
sections.abstract: The authors propose a black-box semantic watermark whose output distribution is unchanged on average over its secret key and demonstrate transformation-robust image watermark detection using a learned semantic encoder.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper appears in three arXiv categories, including two core categories (cs.LG, cs.CV) and cs.CR; it provides a project page and code, and has additional technical coverage from Grafy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors give a model-agnostic construction requiring sampling access and a semantic embedding, then instantiate it for image generators and report robustness to common content-preserving transformations.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction depends on an embedding that is simultaneously stable under content-preserving edits and discriminative between independent generations; the authors train an encoder to address this tradeoff.

sections.title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
sections.abstract: π⁴ jointly estimates 3D geometry, camera pose, scale, point tracks, and moving-object masks from uncalibrated images or video, with a shared model of about 0.5B parameters.
sections.ranking_evidence: The authors provide code and models, and the work has a Hugging Face Papers page; the paper reports a broad set of geometry and motion evaluations in one unified system.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine geometry reconstruction and geometry-conditioned motion estimation in a single forward-pass model, reporting the best overall average rank in their geometry evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports training with contexts of at most 64 views, although it demonstrates inference on scenes with thousands of images; generalization beyond the evaluated scenes and benchmarks remains unestablished.

sections.title: GameRealm: Grounding Visual Learning in Interactive Games
sections.abstract: GameRealm is a gameplay dataset with more than 120 million RGB frames and synchronized depth, camera, audio, control, and 3D-trajectory supervision, which the authors use to train visual generation and geometry models.
sections.ranking_evidence: The dataset has a public project page and repository, making its scale and intended research artifacts checkable.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine human-operated capture and agentic exploration to collect synchronized game-native visual, geometric, audio, and action data, and report gains on selected visual-learning tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify finer-grained human/object skeletons, segmentation masks, and instance labels as future data additions; current evaluation is based on the dataset and task suite they report.

sections.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a 375-pair benchmark and scene-state attack for visual-language models, reporting harmful-assistance rates across eight models and limited protection from the text-side and visual moderation defenses they test.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper is cross-listed in vision and AI and received a separate technical write-up from Bitware News.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define a scene-state safety vulnerability, release SceneSafetyBench, and propose S3TA to test whether models infer harmful assistance from visual context.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported benchmark contains 375 image-question pairs and evaluates eight VLMs; its measured attack rates should not be treated as population-wide estimates for all deployments.

sections.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
sections.abstract: Ambient SFT regularizes fine-tuning by matching high-temperature predictions from the frozen pretrained model, and the authors report gains over standard SFT in domain adaptation, instruction tuning, and reasoning.
sections.ranking_evidence: This paper has the broadest core-category cross-list among the selected submissions and reports experiments in three distinct post-training regimes; independent attention signals were comparatively sparse in the sources checked.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a temperature-matching loss that interpolates between ordinary SFT and knowledge distillation, using the pretrained model as a coarse teacher.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper evaluates the method for supervised fine-tuning; the authors describe extension to reinforcement-learning post-training as future work.
